newsitem.title: USA: North American Vaccine's CERTIVA "safe". [CORRECTED 19:20 GMT]
newsitem.headline: North American Vaccine's CERTIVA "safe". [CORRECTED 19:20 GMT]

text.p: North American Vaccine Inc said its CERTIVA vaccine has been declared "safe and effective" for administration in infants by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration's Vaccines and Related Biological Products Advisory Committee.
(Corrects to clarify FDA Advisory Committee making declaration, not FDA itself)

North American Vaccine said the FDA Advisory Committee concluded that CERTIVA, the company's combined diphtheria, tetanus and acellular pertussis, or whooping cough, vaccine can be safely administered in infants at two, four, six and 15 to 18 months of age.
